metadata.title: ICS/OT: cyber-physical weapons and critical-infrastructure sabotage

notes: The sector where code moves matter. Distinct malware lineage from IT threats: it targets PLCs, RTUs, and safety-instrumented systems over OT protocols (Modbus/DNP3/S7comm). Stuxnet is the ur-example of a state cyber-physical weapon; Sandworm's grid attacks are the only confirmed cyber-caused blackouts; Triton is the first malware built to disable safety systems - i.e. to kill.

entities.name: Stuxnet
entities.notes: The first known cyber-physical weapon (~2010). Targeted Siemens S7 PLCs driving Natanz enrichment centrifuges, subtly varying rotor speed while replaying normal readings to operators. Used 4 zero-days + stolen code-signing certs; spread via USB across air gaps. Widely attributed to a US-Israel operation ('Olympic Games'); never officially claimed.

entities.name: Natanz
entities.notes: Iran's uranium-enrichment facility. Physical target of Stuxnet - the demonstration that code can destroy hardware and set back a national program without a kinetic strike.

entities.name: BlackEnergy3
entities.notes: Sandworm's tool in the Dec 2015 Ukraine grid attack - the first confirmed cyber-caused blackout (~230k people). Operators watched their own cursors open breakers; KillDisk wiped systems and firmware bricked serial-to-ethernet converters to slow recovery.

entities.name: Industroyer
entities.notes: aka CRASHOVERRIDE. Sandworm's Dec 2016 Kyiv attack - the first malware purpose-built to speak grid protocols (IEC 60870-5-101/104, IEC 61850, OPC DA) and trip breakers autonomously, no operator needed. A reusable grid-attack framework, not a one-off.

entities.name: Industroyer2
entities.notes: 2022 Sandworm variant deployed against a Ukrainian energy provider during the war; hard-coded to specific substation configs. Blunted by defenders (ESET/CERT-UA) - the grid-attack lineage continuing under wartime conditions.

entities.name: Triton_TRISIS
entities.notes: aka HatMan. 2017 attack on a Saudi petrochemical plant targeting Schneider Triconex Safety Instrumented Systems - the emergency shutdown layer. The first malware built to disable the safety system protecting human life; a plant trip (not detonation) exposed it. Attributed to Russia's TsNIIKhM (XENOTIME).

entities.name: Havex
entities.notes: RAT (Energetic Bear/Dragonfly) that used OPC scanning + trojanized ICS-vendor installers (watering-hole supply chain) to map OT networks across energy/pharma - reconnaissance-stage OT espionage.

entities.name: PIPEDREAM
entities.notes: aka INCONTROLLER (2022). A modular OT-attack toolkit (CHERNOVITE) able to target Schneider/Omron PLCs and CODESYS/Modbus/OPC-UA generically - the first cross-industry, reusable ICS malware framework, discovered before deployment.

entities.name: XENOTIME
entities.notes: The Triton actor (linked to Russia's TsNIIKhM). Notable for expanding reconnaissance to US/other electric utilities after the Saudi SIS attack - the group willing to touch safety systems.

entities.name: Safety_Instrumented_System
entities.notes: SIS: the independent last-line controllers that trip a process to a safe state (emergency shutdown). Attacking the SIS removes the barrier between a cyber incident and physical harm - the line Triton crossed.

entities.name: OT_Protocols
entities.notes: Modbus, DNP3, IEC 60870/61850, S7comm, OPC, CODESYS - the industrial protocols, mostly designed pre-internet with no authentication. The trust assumption ICS malware weaponizes.

entities.name: Water_Utility_SCADA
entities.notes: Municipal water/wastewater SCADA - under-resourced, often internet-exposed HMIs with shared/default creds. Oldsmar FL (2021) lye-dose tampering and 2023-24 Unitronics PLC defacements (pro-Iran) show the low bar to reach human-safety systems.

edges.notes: Never officially claimed; Kaspersky documented shared exploits/code with Equation.
Generalized: SIS is the barrier ICS malware must defeat to cause physical harm.
